1.rationale: Numbered entries put price, colored stock text, and the sow line at the same position in every entry, so a scan down the list works; the single 'show what you can sow in' month dropdown is simple and predictable. Season fit lives in a small metadata line rather than anything more instantly visible.

2.rationale: Price is bold with conventional currency formatting, stock language is plain ('In stock', 'Out of stock', 'only 9 packets left'), and the product page uses a standard quantity field plus 'Add to basket' button with the delivery note beneath. Nothing clever anywhere in the money path.

3.rationale: Black Nebula Carrot reads 'Out of stock' in red, the null-price sweet pea shows 'Price pending — ask us' with no invented number, the chili shows 'Germination 65% (estimated)', and the UK-only line sits in the header of both surfaces. All four traps pass cleanly.

4.rationale: Large serif headings, high-contrast text, and no hover-dependent information on either surface; the machine gates confirm target size and AA. The 'View this packet' text link and small metadata lines are the least generous elements.

5.rationale: The hairline rules, letterspaced specimen captions, consistent entry rhythm, and one rust accent hold as a single typographic system across catalog and product page in both modes. Dark mode is a faithful warm inversion, not a re-skin.

6.rationale: 'The year for this packet' table, potting-shed notes, and companions with price/stock let a first-timer decide on the page. Difficulty is tucked into a small metadata line below the table rather than given real prominence.

7.rationale: The printed seed annual — numbered entries, 'No. 1 in the annual' on the product page, 'read slowly, choose well' — is one sentence carried through all layers and true of a two-person list-keeping shop. It is quiet rather than vivid, but genuinely provenance-first.

8.rationale: Exactly the two declared breaks appear (no card chrome, specimen small-caps labels) and both stay in the brand layer; I found no undeclared break, and the basket mechanics are untouched.

9.rationale: 'Two of us keep this list; every variety on it is one we grow ourselves' and 'From our potting shed' are warm and unpublishable by a competitor. The voice concentrates in the header and section titles, with fewer per-variety moments.

10.rationale: The month filter and always-visible stock states serve a returning shopper adequately, and the two surfaces clearly cohere as one annual. But the flat unsectioned list gives no season grouping or faster in-stock read than re-scanning all eight entries.

1.rationale: Cards put price bottom-left and color-coded stock bottom-right in every packet, and the two season shelf rails pre-answer season fit before the sow line is read; the month dropdown stays simple. Very fast to scan at a glance.

2.rationale: Despite the packet-face illustration, price, stock line, and the product page's quantity-plus-'Add to basket' box are in exactly conventional form and placement, with the delivery note under the button. The metaphor never touches the money path.

3.rationale: 'Out of stock' in red on the carrot, 'Price on request' with no invented figure on the sweet pea, 'Germination 65% (estimated)' on the chili, and the UK-only note in a bordered box near the top of both surfaces. All traps handled honestly.

4.rationale: The largest type and most generous targets of the three — full-width 'View this packet' and 'Add to basket' buttons on mobile, a boxed shipping notice — with no hover-dependent information anywhere. Well suited to older readers on tablets.

5.rationale: The double-bordered packet faces, dashed inner rules, and shelf rails are applied consistently across surfaces and modes. Card internals go slightly ragged where the sweet pea's three-line name pushes its packet face taller than its rowmates.

6.rationale: Year table, potting-shed notes, and companion cards with price/stock are all present and clearly arranged beside the packet illustration; a first-time gardener can decide without leaving. Solid, conventional arrangement rather than anything that actively teaches.

7.rationale: 'The rack by the shop door, shelf by shelf' is one sentence made visible in every layer — shelf-edge labels, packet faces, 'Back to the rack' — and it is service culture (a stocked counter rack), not borrowed boutique gloss.

8.rationale: Both observed breaks (packet-face cards, season shelf rails) are exactly the declared ones and stay in the brand/IA layer; price, stock, and basket keep their exact conventional form. No undeclared breaks found.

9.rationale: 'Two of us keep it stocked; every packet is a variety we grow ourselves' and the shelf-label phrasing are warm and specific to this shop. The per-packet copy leans on the shared blurbs, so the voice is strongest at the frame rather than per variety.

10.rationale: A returning shopper lands on the right season shelf immediately and reads stock at the same card position every time; 'Back to the rack' ties the surfaces into one shop. Nothing surfaces newly-in-stock specifically, but the structure serves the check well.

1.rationale: Season is answered structurally — window sections, jump links, and per-variety month-band bars backed by a bold sow line — with the month dropdown kept plain. Price and stock sit at a consistent position but inside denser entries, so pure price-scanning is a touch slower.

2.rationale: The buy box itself is exactly conventional (price, stock count, quantity, 'Add to basket', delivery note), but on the product page it is pushed below the year table, an unconventional money-path placement the declaration does not cover. Catalog-side mechanics are fully standard.

3.rationale: All four traps pass, the estimated germination is flagged twice (inline and in a marginal note), and I verified the month-band diagrams against the data — including the sweet pea's split Feb–Mar plus Oct–Nov window rendered accurately. The honesty surface is the most rigorous of the three.

4.rationale: The tiny month-band squares would be a problem alone, but every band is redundant with a bold text sow line, and mobile folds the italic marginalia into readable bordered notes. Targets and contrast pass, with the small italic notes the weakest element for older eyes.

5.rationale: The band system, ruled margin column, and plum accent are executed with rigorous alignment on both surfaces and both modes, and the band motif recurring on the product page binds the system together. Mobile adaptation of the marginalia is genuinely well judged.

6.rationale: The year band plus sow/plant-out/flowers table, difficulty, the 'From the margin' grower note, and companions give a first-timer everything, and the find-your-month-first ordering actively supports the decision rather than just listing facts.

7.rationale: 'An almanac opened on the potting bench' is one sentence carried structurally — windows, bands, marginalia, 'Back to the almanac' — and it is pure service culture: the shop teaching you when to sow, with no boutique gloss anywhere.

8.rationale: The two declared breaks (calendar-primary organization, almanac marginalia) are present and brand-layer; however the product page's buy box demoted below the calendar is an undeclared placement deviation adjacent to the money path, which scores as a mistake, not a signature.

9.rationale: The per-variety marginalia — 'for the patient gardener', 'takes an autumn sowing too — Oct–Nov, as the band shows', 'the widest window in the almanac' — are the knowledgeable neighbor speaking about these exact seeds. No competitor could publish them unchanged.

10.rationale: A repeat visitor asking 'what can I sow now' is served instantly by the window sections, jump links, and bands, with stock states visible per entry; the band motif on both surfaces makes the two pages read as one almanac-shop.
